items.headline: Man jailed 14 weeks for slapping a four-year-old boy at a Woodlands bus stop
items.summary: Muhammad Firdhaus Mokhtar was sentenced on 30 September to 14 weeks’ jail after slapping a four-year-old who had made a rude gesture at him, knocking the boy down. He pleaded guilty to voluntarily causing hurt and was ordered to pay S$170 in compensation.

items.headline: Motorist who ran a red light and dragged a pregnant woman jailed 13 months
items.summary: A 62-year-old driver was jailed for 13 months after running a red light at a pedestrian crossing, striking a pregnant woman and dragging her along the road before he stopped.

items.headline: Lorry driver jailed 23 months over a crash that disabled a cabby who later died
items.summary: A 51-year-old lorry driver was sentenced to 23 months’ jail over a collision that left a 56-year-old taxi driver permanently disabled; the cabby died about two years later.

items.headline: Supreme Court rules out a blanket firecracker ban for Delhi-NCR before Diwali
items.summary: A bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and P.B. Varale said it would neither impose a total ban nor allow round-the-clock bursting, and will weigh permitting CSIR-NEERI ‘green’ crackers during set hours. The matter was posted for further hearing on 15 October.

items.headline: Centre clears rabi crop MSPs with a 17-year-low wheat hike of Rs 25 a quintal
items.summary: The Cabinet set minimum support prices for six rabi crops for 2027-28, raising wheat by just Rs 25 (0.97%) to Rs 2,610 a quintal, the smallest hike since 2010-11, as part of a Rs 2.79 lakh crore package. Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan cited ample wheat stocks.

items.headline: India’s 2026 monsoon ends 13% below normal, officially a drought year
items.summary: The June-September southwest monsoon closed about 13% below normal, the fourth-lowest shortfall since 2001 and a level classified as drought, amid El Nino conditions. It is distinct from the recent flooding in north India and Nepal.

items.headline: Ranchi court frames money-laundering charges against Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren
items.summary: A PMLA court framed charges against sitting Chief Minister Hemant Soren in the 8.86-acre Bargai land case; he appeared by video, pleaded not guilty and called the case baseless. The next hearing is on 30 November.

items.headline: Delhi High Court rejects bail for Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in 2020 riots case
items.summary: The court refused bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA ‘larger conspiracy’ case tied to the February 2020 Delhi riots, keeping them in custody after more than five years.

items.headline: Independent commission finds Manchester City guilty of 114 of 115 financial charges
items.summary: A Premier League independent commission found Manchester City in breach of 114 of 115 financial-rule charges covering 2009-10 to 2017-18, including sponsorship arrangements said to have inflated revenue by about £900m. City said they were disappointed and are expected to appeal; sanctions are yet to be decided.

items.headline: Thousands of prisoners in England and Wales begin early release to ease overcrowding
items.summary: Under the Sentencing Act 2026, inmates on standard determinate sentences started being freed as early as a third of the way through their terms, with up to 5,000 affected. PM Andy Burnham excluded manslaughter, death-by-dangerous-driving and some sex offenders after a public backlash.

items.headline: UK economy grew 0.5% in the second quarter, revised up from 0.4%
items.summary: The Office for National Statistics revised April-June GDP growth up to 0.5% from an initial 0.4%, after 0.6% in the first quarter, and lifted the annual rate to 1.4%.

items.headline: Bank of England warns of spillover risk from hedge-fund leverage in gilts
items.summary: In its Financial Stability Report the Bank of England said high hedge-fund leverage in the gilt market, alongside AI-asset and corporate-debt exposures, raised the risk of stresses crystallising across markets at once.

items.headline: UK’s ‘one in, one out’ migrant returns deal with France lapses without renewal
items.summary: The pilot scheme, under which some Channel arrivals were returned to France in exchange for vetted asylum applicants, expired on 30 September with no extension agreed.

items.headline: Morocco’s king appoints Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as first woman prime minister
items.summary: King Mohammed VI named Marrakesh mayor and housing minister Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, 50, as Morocco’s first female prime minister after her PAM party won 97 of 395 seats in the 23 September election. She becomes the third woman to lead an Arab government and must now build a coalition.

items.headline: Pilot stabs colleague and tries to down an Israel-bound Flydubai jet before passengers intervene
items.summary: On Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, one pilot stabbed the other and appeared to try to crash the aircraft carrying about 174 people before passengers and crew stormed the cockpit. A relief crew landed the jet at Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, which arrested the suspect.

items.headline: MI5 issues first public espionage alert, naming a Chinese institute funding UK research
items.summary: In its first public espionage alert MI5 said the China General Technology Research Institute is a front funding research to boost Chinese intelligence capabilities, and that more than 100 UK-linked academics had contributed to its projects. Security Minister Dan Jarvis wrote to all vice-chancellors.

items.headline: UN Command rules North Korean mines breached the armistice; Kim Yo-jong calls it a farce
items.summary: The UN Command and Seoul concluded that North Korea planted mines that wounded three South Korean soldiers on 21 September, an armistice violation, and demanded an apology. Kim Yo-jong denied any crossing, called the finding a self-staged farce and threatened retaliation.

items.headline: OpenAI in talks to raise over $30bn at a $1.4tn valuation
items.summary: OpenAI is in early talks to raise more than $30bn in a private round valuing it near $1.4tn, a bridge after Sam Altman signalled no 2026 IPO. That would be up from $852bn in March on a revenue run-rate of about $70bn.

items.headline: AI hardware-design startup Flow Engineering raises $50m at a $750m valuation
items.summary: Flow Engineering raised a $50m Series B at a $750m valuation, co-led by Valor Equity Partners and Atreides Management with Sequoia participating. Its customers include Anduril, Rivian, Joby and GM.

items.headline: DoorDash launches a text-to-order AI agent inside Apple Messages
items.summary: DoorDash unveiled an AI ordering agent that works in Apple’s Messages app, matching phone numbers to profiles to reorder favourites and check out with stored payment. It is live in an iOS pilot with 20,000 US users.

items.headline: Data-center supplier Accelevation raises $540m in a Nasdaq IPO priced below range
items.summary: Accelevation and selling holders raised $540m, selling 30 million shares at $18 each, below the $20-24 range; the stock opened at $17.55, valuing the data-center infrastructure firm (ticker ACCV) at about $3.9bn.

items.headline: Micron guides to record $61.5bn revenue as AI memory demand outstrips supply
items.summary: Micron forecast fiscal first-quarter revenue of about $61.5bn and adjusted earnings near $38.15 a share, well above consensus of $57.0bn, citing data-center demand that outstripped supply.

items.headline: China’s factory activity returns to growth as the official PMI rises to 50.1
items.summary: China’s official manufacturing PMI rose to 50.1 in September from 49.8 in August, the first expansion since June, while the non-manufacturing gauge climbed to 50.2 as Beijing rolled out fresh stimulus.

items.headline: Smart-ring maker Oura postpones its Nasdaq IPO, citing market uncertainty
items.summary: Oura shelved an IPO launched on 21 September that sought to raise up to $2.2bn, blaming market uncertainty after some investors balked at the target valuation amid a bond selloff.

items.headline: Dollar posts its best month since June as the euro sinks to a 16-month low
items.summary: The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index rose about 1.9% in September on rising Fed-hike bets and higher Treasury yields, while the euro fell as much as 0.5% to $1.1312, its weakest since May 2025.

items.headline: 🎾 Khachanov stuns second seed Auger-Aliassime in the China Open first round
items.summary: Unseeded Karen Khachanov beat second seed Felix Auger-Aliassime 6-3, 6-3 in the Beijing first round, his second win over the Canadian in under a month and his 18th career top-10 victory.

items.headline: 🎾 Yastremska beats McNally to reach the China Open second round
items.summary: Dayana Yastremska defeated Caty McNally 6-3, 6-4 in the Beijing WTA 1000 first round to improve to 3-0 in their head-to-head, in a draw led by world No. 1 Elena Rybakina.

items.headline: 🏏 Gill’s 223 and Rohit’s 101 power India to a record 406 chase against West Indies
items.summary: India chased down 406 in 43.3 overs to win the Guwahati second ODI by eight wickets and take an unassailable 2-0 series lead. Shubman Gill made an unbeaten 223, the fastest ODI double century, and Rohit Sharma 101 as the pair put on 255; it was the second-highest successful chase in ODI history.

items.headline: 🏎️ F1 heads to Singapore for a first Marina Bay sprint with Antonelli leading
items.summary: Formula 1 returns at the Singapore Grand Prix on 9-11 October, run for the first time as a sprint weekend at the Marina Bay street circuit. Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli leads teammate George Russell by 66 points, 302 to 236, in the title race.

items.headline: Gravitational tug-of-war in Earth’s core is changing the length of our day
items.summary: A Nature study attributes the decades-long, few-millisecond swings in the length of Earth’s day to a gravitational tug-of-war between the solid inner core and the mantle, which makes the inner core slowly deform and wobble on roughly ten-year timescales.

items.headline: Webb spots a metal-poor galaxy cluster that may hold fingerprints of the first stars
items.summary: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers found an overdensity of 17 galaxies with a metallicity about 3% of the Sun’s near a gas cloud at redshift 5.945, whose excess carbon and silicon matches the expected signature of the universe’s first, Population III, stars.

items.headline: Atom-smasher data hint at a phase transition from the early universe
items.summary: Physicists at Brookhaven’s STAR experiment reported an unexpected dip in fluctuations while colliding gold ions to re-create the big bang’s quark-gluon plasma, a possible sign of a long-sought phase transition at some of the densest nuclear matter ever studied.

items.headline: Retatrutide triple-agonist drug drives about 30% weight loss in a phase 3 trial
items.summary: A phase 3 trial of the triple-hormone agonist retatrutide reported average weight loss of roughly 30% of body weight, around 70 pounds, over 80 weeks, with about a third of participants reporting nausea. It is the first such triple agonist to reach phase 3.

fun_fact.headline: The word 'quarantine' means 'forty days'
fun_fact.body: The word “quarantine” comes from the Venetian quaranta giorni — forty days. During the Black Death in the 14th and 15th centuries, Venice forced arriving ships to sit isolated for 40 days before anyone could step ashore. An earlier 30-day rule, the trentino, was stretched to 40 once officials judged that longer was needed to be sure the plague had passed.
fun_fact.source: Wikipedia; CDC Emerging Infectious Diseases journal

puzzle.title: Painted Cube
puzzle.body:
A large cube is built from 27 identical small cubes, stacked 3 × 3 × 3.
The entire outside surface of the large cube is painted red.
The large cube is then taken apart into its 27 small cubes.
How many of the small cubes have paint on exactly TWO of their faces?
puzzle.approach: Sort the 27 small cubes by where they sit — corner, edge, face-centre, or hidden core — and count each group.
puzzle.answer:
12.

Sort the small cubes by position:
• 8 corner cubes — 3 painted faces each
• 12 edge cubes (the middle cube along each of the 12 edges) — exactly 2 painted faces
• 6 face-centre cubes — 1 painted face each
• 1 hidden core cube — 0 painted faces

Check: 8 + 12 + 6 + 1 = 27. The answer is the 12 edge cubes.

word_puzzle.title: Scrambled Basket
word_puzzle.body:
Unscramble each word. All six answers belong to the same category — name it too.

1. GROANE
2. LAPPE
3. NABAAN
4. PAGER
5. CHEAP
6. LUMP
word_puzzle.approach: Each scramble uses every letter exactly once; the six answers share one theme.
word_puzzle.answer:
They are all FRUIT.

1. GROANE → ORANGE
2. LAPPE → APPLE
3. NABAAN → BANANA
4. PAGER → GRAPE
5. CHEAP → PEACH
6. LUMP → PLUM
